title: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Coronagraph Instrument Observation Calibration Plan
extended_summary:
This paper presents a detailed calibration plan for the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Coronagraph Instrument, a technology demonstration intended to enable high-contrast imaging of exoplanets and other faint point sources near bright stars. The central problem is how to remove or control the many sources of error that affect the conversion from detector counts to the planet-to-star flux ratio Fp/Fs, which is the key metric for coronagraphic performance. The paper frames calibration as part of the instrument’s overall flux-ratio noise budget and focuses on observation-based calibration products rather than internal calibration hardware.

The approach is organized around six calibration areas: absolute flux, charge transfer inefficiency, core throughput, flat fields, image corrections, and related processing steps. For each area, the authors describe the purpose, error allocation, current best estimate, observing strategy, and processing concept. The plan relies on on-sky standards and solar-system targets, including HST CALSPEC standard stars for absolute flux, trap-pumping frames for CTI characterization, FSM raster scans for core throughput mapping, Uranus and Neptune for flat-field calibration, and detector calibration sequences for K gain, nonlinearity, EM gain, and cosmic-ray masking.

The context is the Roman Coronagraph’s Technology Demonstration phase, with calibrations designed for on-sky operations and ground-based processing. The paper does not report a participant population in the educational sense, but rather an engineering/instrument context for space-based astronomical observations. Its main conclusion is that the proposed calibration strategy is feasible within the stated error budget, though several elements remain future work and will require additional optimization, especially around sampling patterns, CTI correction for photon-counted data, and calibration cadence.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a technical calibration plan for the Roman Space Telescope coronagraph, not an empirical education study. It contains no peer-reviewed educational intervention evaluation, no participant-level methodology, and no instructional or learner outcomes relevant to the requested taxonomy.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational impact is measured or implied. The paper is about instrument calibration and error budgeting for astronomy, so it has no demonstrable effect on teaching, learning, or school operations.
